(2 comments)
These aren't really requirements of the class, correct?  Can we keep unit tests to expected behavior, and not a test of internal data structures?

Currently `class EntityManager` has around 19 members, some of which are collections or smart pointers.

There is a lot of stuff in EM which can be tested at the unit test level without DBus. My goal is to have a balance of DBus and non-DBus related testing.

That's fine, but doesn't really change my request that the unit tests test the actual function.  Testing that these aren't nullptr doesn't test anything except that they're not nullptr (an internal detail).
Removed a number of these assertions.

Tests like this are just testing internals of EntityManager, not that it has accomplished the task its intended to accomplish.  Unit tests should ideally check to see if the function works as intended.  For example, scannedPowerOff being true might be completely valid as an init state.  It's the dbus interface that matters.

I really do want to see unit tests, if this is what we have so be it, we can iterate.

The unit tests for dbus interfaces come in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/82547

These test might look primitive but they already revealed a memory leak to me which resulted from stopping the `io_context` before the call to object mapper returned which happened in the power status monitor.

Will need to restructure some of the code to make it possible to init an EM without any initial dbus calls.

> I really do want to see unit tests, if this is what we have so be it, we can iterate.

Nice. Then i will have someone to review my works ❤️
Done
All of the other test files here start with test, so this probably should too.
Makes sense, done 👍
And delete it in the destructor?

I was initially concerned about debugging / failed unit test workflow, but yeah, the code can be changed in that workflow to inspect the files.

Added the destructor to delete our temporary directory 👍
This is a change in behavior.  Now this object can be constructed essentially "dead"
Added a separate parameter to the constructor which decides if we want to query the initial power state. So the behavior will be as before in the regular control flow.
I think I commented this somewhere else, but would prefer if we just query it in a separate call.
This isn't a pattern that we'd generally recommend.  If these are public (ie used in a unit test), make them public.

public / private is declaring some *intention* for the rest of `src/`.

I don't believe we can just make everything public just because there is some unit test somewhere.

`public` / `private` is not super useful in a testing context because they prevent us from asserting things we may want to know, without necessarily exposing them to actual API users.

Which is why i use `protected`/`public` and then promote that `protected` to `public` with that neat trick there.


> If these are public (ie used in a unit test), make them public.

A unit test is not a regular API consumer, it's like a second class citizen. I try to avoid messing up things in `src/` for the sake of `test/` if i can avoid it.

> public / private is declaring some *intention* for the rest of `src/`.
> 
> I don't believe we can just make everything public just because there is some unit test somewhere.

We disagree, and that's fine.  I find this form hard to reason about, because I have to look at two different files to trace a unit test.

> 
> `public` / `private` is not super useful in a testing context because they prevent us from asserting things we may want to know, without necessarily exposing them to actual API users.
> 
> Which is why i use `protected`/`public` and then promote that `protected` to `public` with that neat trick there.

Right, and "neat trick" is something that's in conflict with keeping code clear and concise, which is the #1 rule in the coding standard.

This specific pattern is covered pretty clearly in cpp core guidelines under the title "Avoid protected data" so I don't think I'm off base here.  https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#rh-protected

> 
> 
> > If these are public (ie used in a unit test), make them public.
> 
> A unit test is not a regular API consumer, it's like a second class citizen. I try to avoid messing up things in `src/` for the sake of `test/` if i can avoid it.

I think this statement is disputed better by cpp core guidelines than I can do, so please read it, and if you disagree with the advice, or think it doesn't apply, we can continue this conversation.

I don't care as much. I don't think the core guidelines apply much to tests in that specific case since tests should not run into this problem of deep class hierarchies and complicated code.

Changed it to use composition and not use 'protected' anymore. Added a few getter functions to `EntityManager` to be able to read what we need for testing.

> I don't think the core guidelines apply

If this is what you want to do, please make that argument at project level, and we'll see if we can get consensus on "don't use cpp core guidelines for tests". Right now there's no distinction made on test code.

I'm not comfortable with accepting clear violations to cpp core guidelines in this specific case.

> Changed it

Thank you.  Will readd to the review queue.
So now we're not passing the error out?  Not sure what that has to do with adding a unit test?  Probably deserves its own commit and message.
Changed it to pass a separate parameter to the constructor which decides if we wan to query the initial state.

Rather than making this a bool, should we just make the one place where this is constructed just call getInitialPowerStatus() after it's constructed?  Passing in a bool that UT sets one way and normal path sets another way seems like we'll just be missing coverage.
Changed it as suggested 👍

Would really prefer we don't do multiple inheritance here.  Tracking this stuff is a mess, and functionally UniqueSuffix only calls one method.  Just call the method in the class in an override, and do composition rather than inheritence.
Changed it to use composition instead of inheritance.
